title: A sign of unity (Lumen Gentium 1)
hookLine: the Church is a kind of sacrament of unity for all people
tomorrow: a seven-year-old asks where God lives. who answers first?

cards: A field full of folding chairs at a graduation: families who pray five different ways, some who don't pray at all, all clapping for the same kids. The council's document on the Church opens on a crowd bigger than that.

Its first words, Lumen Gentium, mean the light of the nations, and the light it names is Christ, not the Church. The Church comes a breath later, as the place that light shines from. So who is that light for?

teach.h: CHRIST, THE LIGHT OF THE NATIONS.
teach.b: Read the first paragraph in steps. First, the light.
Christ is the light of the nations, and the council longs to bring that light, shining on the face of the Church, to everyone, by preaching the gospel to every creature.
That's Mark's Gospel: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Second, the sentence that names the day.

teach.h: LIKE A SACRAMENT: SIGN AND INSTRUMENT.
teach.b: The Church, it says, is in Christ like a sacrament, a sign and an instrument. Notice the hedge: like a sacrament. Something that works the way a sacrament works, showing a reality and helping bring it about.

teach.h: UNION WITH GOD, AND ALL PEOPLE.
teach.b: Two unions at once: a close union with God, and the unity of the whole human race. Not the unity of one club. The whole human race.
Fourth, why the council said it then.
People, it says, are being drawn closer by social, technical and cultural ties, and it hopes they'll also reach full unity in Christ.
That's a Catholic hope, said in Catholic words. One to tell a friend: the document on the Church doesn't open with the Church at all. It opens with a light meant for everyone.

how: Catholics often quote Lumen Gentium 1 when speaking of the Church's mission to the world and of prayer for unity, including gatherings with Christians of other churches and with people of other faiths.

games.q: what does “a sign of unity” mean?
o: the Church as a lamp showing all people's unity
a road sign pointing the way to the nearest parish
a peace treaty signed by every Christian church

games.q: the first paragraph — tap the pairs.

s: Lumen Gentium opens by talking about the Church
it opens with Christ, the light of the nations; the Church comes next, as the face that light shines on.
the council calls the Church a sign of the unity of the whole human race
a sign and instrument of union with God and of the unity of all people.
Lumen Gentium calls the Church an eighth sacrament
it says like a sacrament: a sign and an instrument, not an eighth rite.

games.q: at a city service for people of many faiths, a speaker says 'one human family, praying different ways.' your cousin calls it watering down the faith. what does Lumen Gentium 1 add?
o: the Church calls itself a sign of the whole human race's unity, while naming Christ as the light.
the Church speaks about unity only among its own members.
the council says every religion is the same, so the differences don't matter.
games.why: Lumen Gentium 1 names Christ as the light and calls the Church a sign of union with God and of the unity of the whole human race: one family, honest differences.

practice: Bring to mind one person on the other side of some line from you: another faith, no faith, an old argument. Send them one short, warm line that asks for nothing back.
If you pray, you can hold them in the same light as yourself while it sends.

wordCard.voice: A sign of unity. Lumen Gentium's picture of the Church: like a sacrament, showing and serving union with God and among all people. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin in Lumen Gentium 1: the Church is like a sacrament, a sign and instrument.

carryVoice: Your line: a sign for all. A lamp held up, not a wall built around. That's the week.

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church

sources.q: Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
